messages:
anna: Heads-up — brought up Stellus customer's LoRA merge onto rwd-base-v2 and ran a quick 50-case QA pack (numeric-extract + instructions).
liam: Nice. Which quant setup did you use? q4f + per-channel symmetric? :eyes:
suresh: We usually try q4f + per-channel for throughput. q4f is the faster 4-bit format we've been testing for low-latency endpoints.
anna: Exactly — q4f per-channel on top of the fused LoRA. Build: `stellus-lora-v1 + rwd-base-v2 -> quant q4f` on dedicated test node in us-west.
anna: Quick run command I used:
```
./mobilize_eval --model rwd-base-v2+stellus-lora:v1 --quant q4f --prompts quickpack50.json --out=/tmp/stellus_q4f.json
```
liam: Cool. Any obvious deltas?
eval-bot: AUTO EVAL: 50 prompts executed. Summary: ACC(exact-num)=0.72 -> 0.56 (↓0.16), Instr-follow F1=0.89 -> 0.86 (↓0.03), Hallucination-rate↑ from 0.04 -> 0.14. See /tmp/stellus_q4f.json
suresh: Oof, numeric extraction drop is bad. Could be quantization or merge interaction (scale clipping in LoRA merge). Did you run fp16 baseline on same prompts?
anna: Yup — fp16 baseline (no quant) with same LoRA: ACC=0.74. So baseline ok; big delta appears when q4f enabled.
liam: Two hypotheses: 1) q4f kernel rounding for small-weight adapter updates; 2) KV cache numeric rounding on long context. Any per-layer deltas?
anna: I dumped per-layer l2 between fused and quantized weights — differences concentrated in final feedforward and layernorm scales.
suresh: Layernorm scale sensitivity would explain numeric output drift. Quick mitigation: try quantization with preserved layernorms (skip LN) or higher-precision for last N layers.
anna: I re-ran with `--quant q4f --skip-layernorm` patch; results:
```
ACC=0.70, Instr-F1=0.88, Hallucination=0.06
```
anna: Much better — still slightly lower than baseline but acceptable for canary.
liam: Good troubleshooting. For Redwood routing we should add a fallback policy: if ACC < 0.68 on quickpack50, route that customer to fp16 until we ship a safe quant profile.
suresh: Agreed. I can add a candidate profile that keeps last 4 transformer blocks at INT8 (or fp16) while q4f for the rest. Also add an eval-gate in the model config.
anna: I'll open a small PR with the eval-gate thresholds and include the quickpack50 outputs and notes about `--skip-layernorm` as an intermediate workaround.
liam: Also schedule a longer 500-case regression later. For now canary to 5% traffic with fallback is fine.
anna: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/812 — includes logs and per-prompt diffs. Please review.
suresh: Reviewing now. If we see anything else weird, we should capture token-level traces for the first failing examples.
liam: Thanks folks. Will update routing and create the rollout playbook (canary, monitor ACC & hallucination metric, rollback threshold). :thumbsup:
anna: tagging @support on the plan and adding a note to the Stellus customer ticket about potential short-term fp16 routing.
liam: perfect. end.
